problems.statement: The C library, through `localtime_r` and `mktime` calls in `rinzler` and `rinzler_proxy` (`src/rinzler/harmony.cpp`, `rust/minijinja/src/lib.rs`).
problems.code_says: The reader list is incomplete. `rinzler`, `runtron` and `rinzler_proxy` all call `tron::init_logging`, which sets an spdlog pattern that starts with `%H:%M:%S.%F`. spdlog formats that time with `localtime_r` by default (`pattern_time_type::local`). So the C library also reads `TZ` for every log line, and `runtron` is affected too. The README itself says that `TZ` changes how `rinzler` or `runtron` behaves.
problems.corrected_cell: The C library, through `localtime_r` and `mktime` calls in `rinzler` and `rinzler_proxy` (`src/rinzler/harmony.cpp`, `rust/minijinja/src/lib.rs`), and through the log library `spdlog` in `rinzler`, `runtron` and `rinzler_proxy`. Tron code does not call `getenv` for it.

problems.statement: Sets the time zone of the local date and time that `rinzler` writes into prompts.
problems.code_says: True, but one effect is missing. The time of day at the start of every log line (console and `alderaan.log`) is local time in the same zone, for `rinzler`, `runtron` and `rinzler_proxy`. A reader who changes `TZ` to change prompt dates also shifts the log times.
problems.corrected_cell: Sets the time zone of the local date and time that `rinzler` writes into prompts. This affects `conversation_start_date` in the system message of `gpt-oss` models, the output of `strftime_now` in chat templates, and the `rendered_at` field of a `save_tokens` capture. `RZ_SYSTEM_START_DATE` pins the date. The current time is then not used, and the pinned date is taken as local noon. The time of day in every log line also uses this time zone. Check: the `rendered_at` field of a chat `save_tokens` response shows the date in effect.

notes:
Short version: 9 of the 10 rows are correct, 1 row (`TZ`) is imprecise, and no row is wrong. The `TZ` row leaves out the log time stamps and `runtron`. The corrected `TZ` row is 989 characters long.

Method: read-only. For each name I ran `git grep`, followed the helper functions and constants, and read the code around every read and every set. Nothing was built and no test was run.

Two checks used sources outside the checkout. (1) The spdlog default time type (`pattern_time_type::local`) came from the spdlog 1.17.0 header in the build tree of another checkout on this host. (2) The C library behaviour for `TZ` came from running `date` on this host (glibc 2.35).

Observations that I did not grade as problems, because no statement of the row contradicts the Tron code:
- `TZ`: glibc uses UTC for a zone name that it does not know, and prints no error. `env TZ=Not/AZone date` printed offset +0000 on this host. The tzset(3) manual page says the same for an empty value, and says that an unset value uses `/etc/localtime`. The README rule asks for an "Empty:" clause when empty differs from unset. The Tron code cannot prove this, and the corrected row has no room left.
- `TZ`: one Rust unit test reads `TZ` with `std::env::var` (rust/minijinja/src/lib.rs:892). The sentence "Tron code does not call `getenv` for it" holds for the programs.
- `TRON_TOKENIZE_PY`: an empty value behaves like an unset one (src/rinzler/tokenizers.cpp:450, GNUmakefile:550). The row has no "Empty:" clause, which matches the README rule. The sentence "The text is used as given" does not hold for empty text.
- `TRON_TOKENIZE_PY`: the branch "Failed to load HuggingFace tokenizer" cannot run, because `make_shared` never returns null (src/rinzler/tokenizers.cpp:1893, 1916). So the three conditions of the row are complete.
- `TRON_MAX_MAIN_HELPERS`: the abort comes after the weights are loaded, when the scheduler builds its forward-pass state (h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:1831). "At model load" is close enough.
- `DICE_ETA`: an empty or blank value behaves like an unset one (bin/rinzler:169, bin/runtron:183). The row has no "Empty:" clause, which matches the README rule.
- `RZ_CHAT_TEMPLATE_KWARGS`: the JSON value `null` is accepted and gives no defaults (h/rinzler/rinzler-config.hpp:227). The row calls every non-object invalid.
- `TRON_BOOK_INITIAL_TOKENS`: the largest DMA allocation can cut the book size, or split one append over several books (h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:745, 1071). The row leaves this out.
